decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core practice software with its own product presence and clear fit with digital workflows in dental practices, it is likely to remain strategically relevant.
Training and continuing education support customer retention and match the firm's support-oriented model, even if this offer is somewhat less central than the software itself.
A remote support tool directly strengthens the firm's customer service capabilities and complements its installed software base, so it is more likely to be maintained than discontinued.
Practice analytics fits the firm's direction toward more digital and efficiently managed healthcare practices and is a natural higher-value add-on to its core system.
A complete practice bundle is very close to the established business and likely serves as a core packaging and sales vehicle rather than a disposable side product.

A job and practice listing portal is the most distant from the firm's core software business and therefore the most plausible candidate to exit if management refocuses resources on stronger strategic fits.
